column3: The Hebrew places Ehud’s death after the statement about Israel’s renewed evil, joined by “and.” BSB places it first as an explicit “After” clause.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the possessor of the chariots unnamed; BSB supplies “Jabin.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew introduces the divine command with the question “Has not the LORD ... commanded?” BSB uses the assertion “Surely ... is commanding.”
The Hebrew explicitly says “to you, to the torrent Kishon”; BSB retains the river destination but leaves “to you” implicit.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the speaker of the reply unnamed until the following narrative clause; BSB identifies her as Deborah within the reply.
The Hebrew explicitly repeats Barak and Kedesh; BSB uses “he” and “where.” It says ten thousand men went up “at his feet,” rendered “followed him” in BSB.
The Hebrew names an oak at Zaanannim; BSB uses the more general “great tree.”
The Hebrew actively says “they told Sisera,” without identifying the speakers; BSB changes this to passive “Sisera was told.”
The Hebrew explicitly names Sisera; BSB uses “he.” It separately says “all his chariots” and then specifies nine hundred iron chariots, which BSB combines.
Close to the Hebrew.

The Hebrew explicitly says “before Barak,” where BSB uses “in front of him.” It names the chariots themselves rather than BSB’s “charioteers” and says Sisera “got down from” the chariot rather than “abandoned” it.
The Hebrew’s sword expression literally says “the mouth of the sword”; BSB has “by the sword.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed, where BSB supplies “Sisera.” It names a milk skin rather than a general “container” and has no separate word for “again.”
Close to the Hebrew.

The Hebrew puts Jael’s actions first and the account of his sleeping and exhaustion afterward; BSB puts the latter first as a causal circumstance. The Hebrew leaves him unnamed where BSB supplies Sisera.
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats the full name and title “Jabin king of Canaan” at the end; BSB replaces the second occurrence with “him.”
